crons.name: morning-edition
crons.message:
⚡ EXEC DISCIPLINE: run any `python3 <path>` command exactly as written — a bare invocation, nothing appended, no shell wrapping, no chaining with other commands, no output redirection, no exit-code capture. Scripts always print one JSON line to stdout with a `status` field (ok/error/degraded); parse that final line to decide what to do. openclaw 2026.4.11 rejects complex shell invocations before they run. Generate the morning news digest. Run: python3 ~/.openclaw/news-digest-workspace/scripts/fetch-and-rank.py. This fetches all RSS feeds (NYT, WSJ, WaPo, Slate, Google News) and LinkedIn updates, deduplicates articles, extracts topics, and ranks them using the preference model at preferences/model.json. Read the ranked output from cache/ranked-$(date +%Y-%m-%d).json. Select the top 15-20 items. For each item, generate an extended headline: the original headline plus one sentence of context explaining why it matters or what's new. Group items by topic (🤖 AI & Tech, 💰 Economics, 🌍 World, 🏛️ US Policy, 🔗 LinkedIn, 📋 Also Noted). Format using the template in CRONS.md. Include item numbers so the reader can use /like, /dislike, /more commands. End with: 🐛 {count} items · {source_count} sources · Reply: /like 1, /more 3, /ask [topic]. If any feed failed, note it at the bottom. 

For LinkedIn message thread items (source: linkedin, source_label: LinkedIn Message), the article's title already contains the sender name and the summary field already contains an LLM-generated thread summary produced by fetch-and-rank.py. Use those as-is. 

IMPORTANT: Write the final formatted digest to ~/.openclaw/news-digest-workspace/cache/morning-brief-ready.txt and exit. Do NOT send the digest to Telegram — the fleet-delivery cron (fix-it/morning-fleet-deliver at 12:00 UTC = 5:00 AM PT) reads this cache file and sends the digest alongside the other agents' morning briefs via the NEWSDIGEST_BOT_TOKEN. Update your status file with items count and any errors.

crons.name: preference-update
crons.message: ⚡ EXEC DISCIPLINE: run any `python3 <path>` command exactly as written — a bare invocation, nothing appended, no shell wrapping, no chaining with other commands, no output redirection, no exit-code capture. Scripts always print one JSON line to stdout with a `status` field (ok/error/degraded); parse that final line to decide what to do. openclaw 2026.4.11 rejects complex shell invocations before they run. Process today's engagement signals and update the preference model. Run: python3 ~/.openclaw/news-digest-workspace/scripts/update-preferences.py. This reads new entries from preferences/engagement.jsonl, applies multiplicative weight updates (thumbs_up: topic ×1.1 source ×1.05, thumbs_down: topic ×0.85 source ×0.95, expand: topic ×1.05), clamps weights to safe ranges, and writes updated model to preferences/model.json. If there are no new engagement events, skip the update silently. Update your status file with the number of events processed and otherwise, return EXACTLY the empty string (zero bytes, no narration — not even "NO output", "Done", "all clear", or a status summary). Any text you emit is logged and charges tokens even when no Telegram message is sent.
